data.title: I forced myself to spend a week in Instagram instead of Xcode
data.author: wallflower
data.article_summary: 开发者Daniel Hour强迫自己一周不写代码，专注在Instagram上进行应用营销。他每天发布叙事性内容吸引用户，联系健身工作室和教练寻求合作，并尝试不同形式的创意内容（如FAQ和短信风格广告）。尽管过程艰难且耗时长，他获得了与知名健身平台的合作机会和用户积极反馈。这次实验让他意识到营销与开发同样重要，不能只依赖“酒香不怕巷子深”的理念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：独立开发者在产品开发和营销中的策略与方法

不同观点：
• [rdrd] 分享了内容创作的策略，强调记录想法和与用户互动的重要性，认为真实性是避免竞争的关键。
• [kristianp] 批评使用虚假故事和伪造信息的营销方式，主张通过真实用户反馈来推广产品。
• [nicbou] 支持与用户紧密互动的方法，通过解决实际问题来优化产品内容，认为细节比大功能更重要。
• [upmostly] 提出了一种“SaaS Schedule Sandwich”的时间管理方法，平衡开发和营销的时间分配。
• [yoshyosh] 建议专注于TikTok/Reels等短视频平台，认为这些平台的传播效果优于24小时消失的Stories。
• [nextworddev] 认为独立应用市场已死，必须投入资金才能获得回报。

补充讨论：
• [johannesberlin] 提到了法律风险，提醒开发者注意品牌名称的使用。
• [mattfrommars] 讨论了移动开发的工具选择，提出了对Swift和XCode的担忧，偏好跨平台工具如React Native。
• [alexchantavy] 强调了营销的重要性，认为“Build it and they will come”是错误的观念。

争议焦点：
• 营销手段的争议：是否应该使用虚假信息（如伪造短信）来吸引用户，还是坚持真实用户反馈。
• 工具选择的争议：是否应该使用原生开发工具（如Swift/XCode）还是跨平台工具（如React Native）。

45322819.article_content:
I forced myself to spend a week in Instagram instead of Xcode
This is what happens when you ban yourself from coding
Daniel Hour
Sep 12, 2025
Share
Let’s set the stage:
The Lagree Buddy app has enough quality features that this is an actual, useful thing that I feel comfortable promoting & charging money for.
There are more features I want to build, but they’re bigger features and are still
weeks
from releasing (because I need to QA them in the real world).
Since the hard paywall and overhauled onboarding (
discussed here
), there has been a noticeable increase in purchases (woohoo! see chart below)
Given the information above, I figured I should try an experiment.
What if I spent every business hour on marketing/distribution instead of coding and building more features?
That felt so uncomfortable to even say out loud because it meant spending a week on social media and talking to people about the app. But it also meant not hiding inside the code.
So here’s a detailed (but slightly stream of consciousness) recap of how that week went.
Day 1 || Monday, August 25th
If any influencers out there want to give me some tips on how to IG correctly, please do. But my current thought process is to craft a story arc for one day. And then to break that arc into 4-6 posts, to be posted every 3 hours or so.
I do this because I don’t want it to feel salesy or spammy. So I at least inject some sort of narrative. So today’s story arc was:
Working on new feature at home, but oh no! it’s broken!
Thought I fixed it and took it to class, but oh no! still broken!
I found out why it was broken, explained it, and took it into another class …
FIXED.
FIXED 2.
FIXED 3.
I also spent the day reaching out to new studios & trainers I saw wearing Apple Watches. Sent out 10 today and got 2 responses.
Day 2 || Tuesday, August 26th
I bought a Microformer last week, so let’s use the thing for some content!
I signed up for
Lagreeing at Home
,
found an instructor with an Apple Watch
, snapped a lot of photos, and got busy creating and scheduling another story arc.
I almost
immediately
got a response from Lagreeing at Home about collabing, and I’d have to say… that’s a pretty big win. Lagreeing at Home was born out of the pandemic and has been an incredible presence in the Lagree community, so hearing some affirmation from them is a fantastic feeling.
I wanted to do more cold DM’s to studios and trainers today, too, but sometimes the Apple Gods say “try again tomorrow” (wheel of death! see below).
Day 3 || Wednesday, August 27th
It’s only been two days, but I’ve been struggling with the actual creation of content itself. Struggling might be the wrong word… underestimate? I underestimated the amount of work it takes!
I planned everything out on Monday. But then you have to obviously create the stuff, and all of that takes so long! So today, today is going to be an FAQ series. But the question is how to create it
creatively
so it’s not just social media slop.
And after playing with a basic Q&A and not liking how it looked (aka ugly and sales-y) ... I went hunting on Reddit and found this
incredible tool (Postfully
) to create fake text messages and came up with this for my Q&A instead:
Day 4 || Thursday, August 28th
I signed up for
THE Sebastian Lagree’s class
on Sunday. Three reasons why:
I want to show him the app in person
I’m running out of content and I need some photos of a new studio 😅
I’m getting sick of social media and wanted to do something in real life loll
I needed a break from creating content, so I cheated and repurposed my IG stories into
TikTok videos
. But I didn’t want to give up on my mission, so I fell back on cold messaging studios and trainers.
Getting any response is a nice feeling, but this message back from new studio
Hold Fitness
was incredible! She saw my
original post on Reddit
from 6 months ago!
I have been messaging new studios and offering promo codes for their grand openings!
Day 5 || Friday, August 29th
I am absolutely ITCHING to get back to the code!!
But I am trying to stick to my mission for the week and am racking my brain on what content to come up without sounding repetitive or spammy. Thank goodness I went to class yesterday and took a bunch of b-roll footage because an idea quickly formed that felt different enough from everything before it this week.
This might have been the hardest day to stick to this challenge. Because everything inside of me was screaming:
“CAN WE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD GET OFF OF SOCIAL MEDIA AND DO SOMETHING PRODUCTIVE LIKE BUILD MORE FEATURES.”
But the thing that I had to constantly remind myself of is that
this
is
productive.
Build it and they will come is a fallacy.
You have to tell people about the damn thing. It just doesn’t
feel
productive because you’re over here churning and burning things that feel like they have a shelf-life of 24 hours (if even that). And sending out cold DM’s and hoping for 1 or 2 responses.
Day 6 || Saturday, August 30th
Day of rest.
Sorry, not sorry.
But

data.title: The Beginner's Textbook for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
data.author: Qision
data.article_summary: 这篇论文介绍了全同态加密（FHE）的基础教程，FHE是一种能直接在加密数据上进行计算的密码学方案。FHE支持基本的加法和乘法运算，通过这些运算可以构建更复杂的计算，包括逻辑运算和高级数学函数。FHE可应用于隐私保护的机器学习、机密区块链服务、安全数据分析和加密数据库查询等场景。该书是一个开放项目，欢迎专家参与协作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[全同态加密（FHE）的实际应用、计算开销、以及与零知识证明（ZK）在隐私保护机器学习中的潜在结合]

不同观点：
• **支持FHE在隐私保护ML中的应用**  
  - [logannyeMD]认为ZK证明可以提升隐私保护ML的实用性，但承认FHE的计算开销仍是主要瓶颈。  
  - [EGreg]指出神经网络的微分特性使其可被全同态加密，暗示FHE在加密LLM等场景的潜力。  

• **质疑FHE的普适性与计算可行性**  
  - [Hizonner]提出FHE存在操作次数限制和显著计算开销，质疑其能否支持大规模ML模型。  
  - [sandworm101]强调FHE可能带来100x-1000x的计算负担，担忧其大规模实用性。  

• **探索FHE的其他应用场景**  
  - [hamburgererror]询问FHE是否可用于日常场景（如OS、消息应用）或实现真正混淆，引发对FHE非ML用途的讨论。  

补充讨论：  
• **资源与学习成本**  
  - [inasio]指出论文参考文献较少，可能影响与其他领域的交叉验证。  
  - [karolcodes]提到阅读长篇论文的时间成本问题，反映技术落地的认知门槛。  
• **争议焦点**：FHE的实际计算开销是否足以支持其宣称的应用场景（如大规模ML），以及是否存在未被充分讨论的替代方案（如ZK证明）。

Title:
The Beginner's Textbook for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
Authors:
Ronny Ko
View a PDF of the paper titled The Beginner's Textbook for Fully Homomorphic Encryption, by Ronny Ko
View PDF
Abstract:
Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a cryptographic scheme that enables computations to be performed directly on encrypted data, as if the data were in plaintext. After all computations are performed on the encrypted data, it can be decrypted to reveal the result. The decrypted value matches the result that would have been obtained if the same computations were applied to the plaintext data.
FHE supports basic operations such as addition and multiplication on encrypted numbers. Using these fundamental operations, more complex computations can be constructed, including subtraction, division, logic gates (e.g., AND, OR, XOR, NAND, MUX), and even advanced mathematical functions such as ReLU, sigmoid, and trigonometric functions (e.g., sin, cos). These functions can be implemented either as exact formulas or as approximations, depending on the trade-off between computational efficiency and accuracy.
FHE enables privacy-preserving machine learning by allowing a server to process the client's data in its encrypted form through an ML model. With FHE, the server learns neither the plaintext version of the input features nor the inference results. Only the client, using their secret key, can decrypt and access the results at the end of the service protocol. FHE can also be applied to confidential blockchain services, ensuring that sensitive data in smart contracts remains encrypted and confidential while maintaining the transparency and integrity of the execution process. Other applications of FHE include secure outsourcing of data analytics, encrypted database queries, privacy-preserving searches, efficient multi-party computation for digital signatures, and more.
As this book is an open project (
this https URL
), we welcome FHE experts to join us as collaborators to help expand the draft.

data.title: The Counterclockwise Experiment
data.author: domofutu
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Ellen Langer的"逆龄"研究是否科学可信，以及环境对心理和生理状态的影响]

不同观点：
• **质疑研究的科学性和可重复性**  
  - patel011393和FarMcKon指出Langer的研究存在严重问题，未被独立复现，并链接了PubPeer上的批评（如统计缺陷）。  
  - cadamsdotcom提到心理学领域的"可重复性危机"，暗示此类研究可能属于不可靠案例。  
  - FarMcKon强调"非凡主张需要非凡证据"，认为若研究真实，早应有商业化应用（如"逆龄度假"）。

• **支持环境对心理状态的积极影响**  
  - AvAn12以自身经历为例，认为年轻环境能提升能量和乐观情绪（虽不逆转衰老）。  
  - sandspar观察到父亲回忆青春时短暂的活力重现，佐证心理状态对生理的短暂影响。  
  - daniel-gerow通过安第斯山区老人的例子，说明无意识的社区生活方式可能超越年龄限制。

• **中立或补充视角**  
  - m3047提出"功能性叠加"概念，解释行为模式在伤病愈后仍持续的现象。  
  - ookblah承认衰老需调整行为强度，但强调主观能动性的平衡。  
  - SamBam质疑负面环境（如2020年疫情）是否会产生相反效果，暗示情绪态度的关键作用。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：研究是否属于科学突破（支持方）还是"轶事"（反对方），核心矛盾在于方法论严谨性与实际观察现象的冲突。  
- **其他讨论**：  
  - opminion和nickdothutton将话题延伸至怀旧媒介的影响（如90年代电视）。  
  - sebmellen批评文章文风疑似AI生成，侧面反映科学传播的信任问题。  
  - daniel-gerow和AvAn12的案例被反对方视为"孤证"，但支持方认为其揭示了环境与心态的复杂互动。

iNapGPU 🖥
Text-mode graphics card, using only TTL gates.
Specs
VGA resolution 800x600@60Hz (accessible 400x300), mono
50x18 characters
up to 255 chars in charset, up to 4 charsets using 1Mbit EPROM
created using 2 counters, some TTL gates and EPROM with SRAM
parallel interface; works with arduino or Z80
terrible idea anyway, use fpga instead
total IC count: 21
supports latin alphabet with polish letters, and Standard Galactic Alphabet
Inspired by Ben Eater's "
World's worst video card
", I built myself something more.. worse? His video card was rather a digital frame, than a working video card. I fixed this - and I optimized the timer circuitry.
(anyway, i have to tell you that my english is not best, but i try)
I haven't built a computer yet, so the card is tested with Arduino Mega, as it have many pins and it's quite cheap. So, as long as you have 21 free pins on your microcontroller (or you have hooked some shift registers), you can connect the GPU card to almost anything - Arduino, ESP, STM etc. The test code for Mega is attached in this repository.
Here is how the card looks:
I know it's terrible, and soldering many, MANY connections with .12mm wire is terrible too, but it's how I done it. When I was creating the schematic, I didn't know that it will work - this is why I soldered it on protoboard. I suggest you to
do it on fpga 'cause everyone's life will be easier then
create a normal PCB, DIY or bought.
So - I'll skip the most obvious parts, and focus on the HSYNC timer.
The pixel clock is 20MHz - two times more than Ben's card. Instead of using 3 4bit counters, I used one, 12bit counter. The thing is, it's rated for 12MHz max. at 15V! This is why I DON'T GUARANTEE this will work for you; you should use those 4bit counters. (tip: for me only SMD versions of CD4040 worked) Next, the numbers from counter are going to NAND gates. There are two things with it - I'm comparing only "ones"of numbers, but Ben is comparing the entire number. The thing is, when I'm not comparing "zeros", the number will be "shown" multiple times, what luckily won't affect us. Since the RS flip-flop is activated once, activating it more times won't do anything. Same for resetting it. The signal from last pixel (528) is connected via NOT gate, as reset and clock are high active signals.
With the vertical timer the thing is same: normal CD4040 counter, with NAND gates and two RS flip-flops. And at this stage, I did a small mistake, just as Ben did: the timers are counting from 0. Thus, when the total amount of pixels in a row WILL be 528px, the first pixel is 0, and the last is 527. At least let's say it's not that important, as everything is working just fine. Another thing is, that the timer IS running at 37.(87)kHz, and physically we could achieve resolution 400x600 - but this is really bad idea. This is why the first bit of the counter is not used.
The heart of my GPU is in the last sheet. I've successfully connected RAM and ROM to timers, that generate actual image. I used M27C1001 with read time up to 100ns, and as far as I checked - version 45ns doesn't really change anything. The IC is UV EPROM with capacity of 1Mbit. Sadly, this decreases to "only" 128kbit, as I'm using the memory as 1bit memory. At least, it was enough for 4 charsets with 255 chars each.
The first 8 bits of address is a character from SRAM. The next four bits are rows, next three bits are columns, and last two bits are for chosing the codepage.
Also, you can select the actual color of the font.
As being said, the first 8 bits are connected to the SRAM. I used 2kB HM6116 IC, as I don't need more (there's only 900 chars to store). The tricky thing is connecting the entire card with the environment. I used tri-state logic buffers, 74LS245 and 74LS244 as most optimal choice. They're separating timers from the SRAM while writing, and separating data and address bus while timers are reading from SRAM. Also, I did there a small mistake, and connected '245 between SRAM and EPROM. The best solution here should be a latch, as it will store actual character for a moment, not clear the entire bus. This should work better than '245, but I don't have '373 at this moment.
And this is it! An actual video card from TTL gates, as I said. I'm giving to you tools to convert an image into a charset, and code I used for testing with Arduino.  On
this repository
is also code for my DIY eprom programmer. I hope you won't do this,

data.title: Be careful with Go struct embedding
data.author: mattjhall
data.article_summary: 本文警告Go语言中结构体嵌入(Struct Embedding)功能可能带来的陷阱。文章通过示例说明，当多个嵌入结构体包含相同字段名时，Go会优先访问最外层字段而非报错，这可能导致预期外的行为。作者以实际工作中遇到的类似问题为例，提醒开发者在使用结构体嵌入时要特别小心这种字段名冲突的情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中结构体嵌入（struct embedding）的行为及其合理性

不同观点：
• Go允许不同深度的嵌入结构体存在同名字段，这是有意为之的设计，目的是防止外部库的结构体变更影响现有代码（divan）。例如，外部库未来新增字段不应导致用户代码无法编译。
• 结构体嵌入是一个设计缺陷，应该被限制使用（nemo1618, alpb）。多位开发者表示在实践中经常后悔使用嵌入，认为它容易导致混淆和错误。
• 直接访问嵌入字段（如`opts.URL`）是不明确的，应该强制使用完整路径（如`opts.FooService.URL`）以避免歧义（desumeku）。
• Go的选择器（selector）行为是明确的：优先选择最浅深度的字段（joahnn_s）。这是语言规范的一部分，行为符合预期。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：是否应该允许不同深度的同名字段存在，以及直接访问嵌入字段是否合理。
• 技术细节：编译器通过深度优先搜索处理字段选择，但对同深度的同名字段会报错（tymscar）。
• 实用案例：有开发者表示在某些场景（如AWS客户端封装）中嵌入是唯一清晰的解决方案（lowmagnet）。
• 工具支持：部分IDE能检测这种潜在问题（bilbo-b-baggins）。
• 设计权衡：这是语言设计中的一个微妙权衡，严格限制会影响灵活性（divan）。

Be Careful with Go Struct Embedding
Go has a feature called struct embedding that allows you to compose types. It looks something like this:
type
Position
struct
{
X
int
Y
int
}
type
Colour
struct
{
R
byte
G
byte
B
byte
}
type
Rectangle
struct
{
Position
Colour
Width
int
Height
int
}
r
:=
Rectangle
{
/* ... */
}
// This works:
fmt
.
Printf
(
"%d,%d\n"
,
r
.
Position
.
X
,
r
.
Position
.
Y
)
// but so does this:
fmt
.
Printf
(
"%d,%d\n"
,
r
.
X
,
r
.
Y
)
But what do you think this code does?
type
FooService
struct
{
URL
string
}
type
BarConnectionOptions
struct
{
URL
string
}
type
BarService
struct
{
BarConnectionOptions
}
type
Options
struct
{
FooService
BarService
}
opts
:=
Options
{
FooService
:
FooService
{
URL
:
"abc.com"
},
BarService
:
BarService
{
BarConnectionOptions
:
BarConnectionOptions
{
URL
:
"xyz.com"
,
},
},
}
fmt
.
Println
(
opts
.
URL
)
I would expect this to fail to compile as
URL
is ambiguous. It actually prints
abc.com
, presumably as it is the least nested version of that field. This happened at the day job, although it was caught in a test. Be careful when embedding structs!

data.title: My new Git utility `what-changed-twice` needs a new name
data.author: jamesbowman
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Mark Dominus（陶敏修）的个人博客文章，介绍了自己开发的一个名为`what-changed-twice`（临时命名为Fred）的Git工具。该工具主要用于分析多次修改的文件，帮助用户在多个提交中识别并整理相关的更改。作者还提供了工具的使用示例和输出报告的解释，并邀请读者为工具建议更好的名称。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[工具名称的合理性及改进建议]

不同观点：
• 支持原名"what-changed-twice"：用户认为名称清晰表达了功能（[GuB-42]、[squeaky-clean]），即使技术上可能改变超过两次（"changed-twice"作为最小情况仍成立）。反对"squash-what"等模糊命名（[squeaky-clean]）。
• 建议新名称派系：
  - 功能描述型："group-commits-by-file"（[handsclean]）、"git-repeatedly-changed"（[zahlman]）
  - 动作导向型："git squash-report"（[quuxplusone]）、"git-delta"（[allseeingimei]）
• 命名空间建议：推荐使用"git-"前缀便于记忆和补全（[zahlman]）

补充讨论：
1. 输出格式争议：
   • 当前高缩写ID被质疑冗余（[nferraz]建议直接显示完整ID）
   • 前缀数字可进一步简化（[perfmode]提议"40→4"）

2. 工具功能边界：
   • [gorgoiler]指出该工具实际涵盖多场景（依赖图构建/提交重组/cherry-pick自动化），当前名称仅反映部分功能
   • [eru]提醒文本级无冲突≠语义无冲突（可能破坏测试）

3. 技术实现参考：
   • 类比Jujutsu的"absorb"命令（[codewritero]）
   • 引用"gather"算法处理类似场景（[MontagFTB]）

争议焦点：
• 名称是否应严格准确（如"twice"vs"more-than-once"）
• 功能描述优先vs git命名惯例优先
• 输出信息的精简程度

My new git utility `what-changed-twice` needs a new name
As I have
explained in the past
, my typical workflow is to go
along commiting stuff that might or might not make sense, then clean it
all up at the end, doing multiple passes with
git-add
and
git-rebase
to get related changes into the same commit, and then to order the
commits in a sensible way. Yesterday I built a new utility that I found
helpful.  I couldn't think of a name for it, so I called it
what-changed-twice
, which is not great but my I am bad at naming
things and my first attempt was
analyze-commits
. I welcome
suggestions. In this article I will call it Fred.
What is Fred for?  I have a couple of uses for it so far.
Often as I work I'll produce a chain of commits that looks like
this:
470947ff minor corrections
d630bf32 continue work on `jq` series
c24b8b24 wip
f4695e97 fix link
a8aa1a5c sp
5f1d7a61 WIP
a337696f Where is the quincunx on the quincunx?
39fe1810 new article: The fivefold symmetry of the quince
0a5a8e2e update broken link
196e7491 sp

40c52f47 merge old and new seasons articles and publish
b59441cd finish updating with Star Wars Droids
537a3545 droids and BJ and the Bear
d142598c Add nicely formatted season tables to this old article
19340470 mention numberphile video
It often happens that I will modify a file on Monday, modify it some
more on Tuesday, correct a spelling error on Wednesday. I might have
made 7 sets of changes to the main file, of which 4 are related, 2
others are related to each other but not to the other 4, and the last
one is unrelated to any of the rest. When a file has changed more than

The

Some files changed only once, and I don't need to think about those at
this stage.  Later I can go back and split up those commits if it seems

Fred takes the output of

in:
$ git log --stat -20 main...topic | /tmp/what-changed-twice

report about any file that was modified in more than one commit:

math/centrifuge.blog  193 33
misc/straight-men.blog  53 b5 bd
prog/jq-2.blog  33 5f d6
193  1934047
196  196e749
33  33a2304
40  40c52f4
53  537a354
5f  5f1d7a6
b5  b59441c
bd  bdc781f
d1  d142598
d6  d630bf3
The report is in two parts.  At the top, the path of each file that
changed more than once in the log, and the (highly-abbreviated) commit
IDs of the commits in which it changed.  For example,

changed in commits
196
,
40
, and
d1
.  The
second part of the report explains that
196
is actually an
abbreviation for commit
196e749
.
Now I can look to see what else changed in those three commits:

calendar/seasons.blog

commits

and then decide if there are any changes I might like to squash
together.

myself with four.

data.title: Show HN: Tips to stay safe from NPM supply chain attacks
data.author: bodash
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了防止NPM供应链攻击的安全最佳实践。主要建议包括：开发者应固定依赖版本、包含锁文件、禁用生命周期脚本、设置最小发布年龄、使用权限模型并减少外部依赖；维护者需启用双重认证、创建有限访问令牌、生成来源声明并检查发布文件；其他建议还有使用私有注册表、审计监控工具及支持开源软件。文章涵盖了npm、bun、deno、pnpm和yarn等多种包管理器的安全配置方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[如何防范Node.js和NPM生态中的供应链攻击]

不同观点：
• **反对使用npx**  
  - npx会动态解析依赖，难以追踪实际执行的代码  
  - 导致SBOM（软件物料清单）合规性失效  
  - 举例：2022年colors事件中依赖即时解析引发问题  

• **锁定依赖版本的实践建议**  
  - 推荐使用`npm ci`确保锁文件中的依赖版本（HoyaSaxa）  
  - 建议每日更新依赖（`npm install --before="$(date -v -1d)"`）  
  - GitHub Actions用户应启用Dependabot冷却功能并固定依赖SHA  

• **离线构建与依赖审查**  
  - 通过离线CI/CD（如无网络CI服务器）强制依赖审查（condiment）  
  - 工具尝试：如shrinkpack离线镜像（fold_left）  
  - 手动审查依赖代码（zygentoma）  

• **未被充分讨论的攻击向量**  
  - 全局模块和编辑器扩展自动安装最新版本（abejfehr）  
  - 如eslint/prettier插件可能引入风险  
  - 缺乏对非人类可读代码（如编译JS）的警惕（fergie）  

• **系统性解决方案呼吁**  
  - 需语言级支持（如上下文白名单）（jimbohn）  
  - 期待新安全优先的替代技术栈（dwoldrich）  
  - 工具推荐：Packj检测攻击指标（ashishbijlani）、vet依赖审查（indigodaddy）  

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：是否需固定所有依赖版本（Rockslide认为锁文件已足够）  
- **开发环境隔离**：Docker化本地开发以降低风险（aiahs）  
- **极端建议**：完全自研或彻底审查依赖（lrvick）  
- **团队协作配置**：通过yarnrc统一团队设置（aetherspawn）

NPM Security Best Practices
Note
The NPM ecosystem is no stranger to compromises
1
2
, supply-chain attacks
3
, malware
4
5
, spam
6
, phishing
7
, incidents
8
or even trolls
9
. In this repository, I have consolidated a list of information you might find useful in securing yourself against these incidents.
Feel free to submit a Pull Request, or reach out to me on
Twitter
!
Tip
This repository covers
npm
,
bun
,
deno
,
pnpm
,
yarn
and more.
Table of Contents
For Developers
1. Pin dependency versions
2. Include lockfiles
3. Disable lifecycle scripts
4. Set minimal release age
5. Permission Model
6. Reduce external dependencies
For Maintainers
7. Enable 2FA
8. Create tokens with limited access
9. Generate provenance statements
10. Review published files
Miscellaneous
11. Use private registry
12. Audit, monitor and security tools
13. Support OSS
For Developers
1. Pin Dependency Versions
On
npm
, by default, a new dependency will be installed with the Caret
^
operator. This operator installs the most recent
minor
or
patch
releases. E.g.,
^1.2.3
will install
1.2.3
,
1.2.4
,
1.3.0
,
1.6.2
, etc. See
https://docs.npmjs.com/about-semantic-versioning
and try out the npm SemVer Calculator (
https://semver.npmjs.com
). To avoid installing freshly compromised packages, it is often advised to pin exact versions (e.g.,
"my-package": "1.2.3"
).
Here's how to use the save exact flag to pin exact version in various package managers:
npm install --save-exact react
pnpm add --save-exact react
yarn add --save-exact react
bun add --exact react
deno add npm:react@19.1.1
We can also update this setting in configuration files (e.g.,
.npmrc
), with either
save-exact
or
save-prefix
alike key and value pairs:
npm config
set
save-exact=true
pnpm config
set
save-exact
true
yarn config
set
defaultSemverRangePrefix
"
"
For
bun
, the config file is
bunfig.toml
and corresponding config is:
[
install
]
exact
=
true
Override the transitive dependencies
However
, our direct dependencies also have their own dependencies (
transitive
dependencies). Even if we pin our direct dependencies, their transitive dependencies might still use broad version range operators (like
^
or
~
). The solution is to override the transitive dependencies:
https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json#overrides
In
package.json
, if we have the following
overrides
field:
{
"dependencies"
: {
"library-a"
:
"
^3.0.0
"
},
"overrides"
: {
"lodash"
:
"
4.17.21
"
}
}
Let's assume that
⁠library-a
's
⁠package.json
has a dependency on
"lodash": "^4.17.0"
Without the
⁠overrides
section,
⁠npm
might install
⁠lodash@4.17.22
(or any of the latest
⁠4.x.x
versions) as a transitive dependency of
⁠library-a
However, by adding
"overrides": { "lodash": "4.17.21" }
, we are telling
⁠npm
that anywhere
⁠lodash
appears in the dependency tree, it must be resolved to exactly version
⁠4.17.21
For
pnpm
, we can also define the
overrides
field in the
pnpm-workspace.yaml
file:
https://pnpm.io/settings#overrides
For
yarn
, the
resolutions
field is introduced before the
overrides
field, and it also offers a similar functionality:
https://yarnpkg.com/configuration/manifest#resolutions
{
"resolutions"
: {
"lodash"
:
"
4.17.21
"
}
}
#
yarn also provide a cli to set the resolution: https://yarnpkg.com/cli/set/resolution
yarn
set
resolution
<
descriptor
>
<
resolution
>
For
bun
, it supports either the
overrides
field or the
resolutions
field:
https://bun.com/docs/install/overrides
For
deno
, see
denoland/deno#28664
for more details.
2. Include Lockfiles
Ensure to commit package managers lockfiles to
git
and share between different environments. Different lockfiles are:
package-lock.json
for
npm
,
pnpm-lock.yaml
for
pnpm
,
bun.lock
for
bun
,
yarn.lock
for
yarn
and
deno.lock
for
deno
.
In automated environments such as continuous integration and deployments, we should install the exact dependencies as defined in the lockfile.
npm ci
bun install --frozen-lockfile
yarn install --frozen-lockfile
deno install --frozen
For
deno
, we can also set the following in a
deno.json
file:
{
"lock"
: {
"frozen"
:
true
}
}
3. Disable Lifecycle Scripts
Lifecycle scripts are special scripts that happen in addition to the
pre<event>
,
post<event>
, and
<event>
scripts. For instance,
preinstall
is run before
install
is run and
postinstall
is run after

is run. See how npm handles the "

data.title: Obsidian Note Codes
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为“Note Codes”的Obsidian插件，它可以为库中的每个笔记生成一个4字符的唯一代码，便于快速引用。代码由字母和数字组成，排除了容易混淆的字符（如O、I等），并支持协议处理（如`obsidian://note-codes/open?code=XX-XX`）。代码基于笔记的名称和路径生成，若笔记重命名，代码会随之改变。作者还提到，插件使用SHA-256哈希和Base32编码确保唯一性，并开源在GitHub上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[4字符编码的唯一性、生成方式及其在Obsidian中的实用性]

不同观点：
• **编码唯一性不足**：sethaurus指出32^4（1,048,576）种组合在实际使用中不足以避免冲突，特别是在笔记数量较多时（如500笔记时有10%的冲突概率）。他认为需要通过分配唯一ID来解决这一问题。
• **编码生成方式不合理**：1dom和usiusi质疑编码基于文件名和路径的设计，认为这会因文件重命名或移动导致编码变化，影响使用体验。usiusi建议改用UUID或创建时间戳来生成固定编码。
• **编码的实际用途**：quantike和yyx对编码的实际用途提出疑问，认为Obsidian已支持直接链接笔记，编码的附加价值不明确。yyx指出可以直接使用obsidian://open链接。
• **编码生成改进建议**：varun_ch提出可以根据标题生成更具语义的编码（如M5-LM），并探讨LLM可能的应用。Igrom建议借鉴Git的短哈希前缀方法，通过唯一前缀避免冲突。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现争议**：link0php关注编码在文件移动后的更新问题，以及同名文件可能引发的冲突。sfkgtbor分享了使用Python生成4字符编码的实际应用（如标记物理物品）。
• **其他工具的比较**：precompute和4b11b4提到类似功能的其他工具（如org-id和roam），暗示现有解决方案可能更成熟。
• **设计选择批评**：GlacierFox批评了编码与文件名绑定的设计，计划改用GUID实现类似功能。

45288739.article_content:
Obsidian Note Codes
🦔 🦔 🦔
Obsidian with the Note Code plugin on the bottom right showing the code for a note about hedgehogs.
I made a little plugin for Obsidian:
Note Codes
.
It will assign a 4-character code to every note in your
Obsidian
vault. Those codes let you quickly reference notes in your vault from other places such as hand-written notes.
Click here to try it out.
To make things nicer, there's also a protocol handler, so something like
obsidian://note-codes/open?code=XX-XX
will open the note with the code
XX-XX
.
I tried to make these codes look nice even if they are handwritten. They're just four characters and some of the similar-looking ones are removed (though the plugin is smart enough to know that
AA-0A
is the same as
AA-OA
.
As usual, it's all open source:
https://github.com/SilverEzhik/obsidian-note-codes
What's in a note code?
Note codes are generated based on a note's name and path, meaning that the note code will change if you rename your note.
Each note code consists of 4 alphanumeric characters. For clarity,
O
,
I
,
L
, and
U
are excluded from the codes, but this plugin will automatically handle these correctly - so
OI-LU
will automatically be treated as
01-1V
when searching. Same with the missing dash or lowercase letters.
Note codes are generated by SHA-256-hashing the note's path in the vault, then taking the first 20 bits of the hash and encoding them using
Douglas Crockford's Base32 encoding scheme
.
32^4 = 1,048,576, which is hopefully enough.

• **技术实现争议**：link0php关注编码在文件移动后的更新问题，以及同名文件可能引发的冲突。sfkgtbor分享了使用Python生成4字符编码的实际应用（如标记物理物品）。

  - 举例：数据路由和隐私问题同样存在于物理SIM卡中。
  - 争议焦点：标题是否误导，将商业问题归咎于技术。

• **运营商限制和费用**
  - 用户担心eSIM被运营商用于限制预付费手机或收取额外费用。

  - 争议焦点：eSIM是否被滥用为控制工具。

  - 提到中国对eSIM的严格限制，引发对安全漏洞的猜测。
  - 举例：用户发现IP被路由到香港，引发隐私担忧。
  - 争议焦点：eSIM是否存在未公开的安全漏洞。

• **解决方案**
  - 一些用户建议使用VPN（如Wireguard或Tor）来缓解路由风险。
  - 推荐特定eSIM提供商（如Google Fi）以减少问题。

• **实际使用体验**
  - 用户分享旅行中使用eSIM的正面和负面经历。
  - 争议焦点：eSIM在实际使用中是否比物理SIM卡更方便。

data.title: DSM Disorders Disappear in Statistical Clustering of Psychiatric Symptoms (2024)
data.author: rendx
data.article_summary: 这项研究通过数据驱动的方法对DSM-5精神病理症状进行重组，挑战了传统的精神障碍分类方式。研究人员对14,800名参与者进行了随机顺序的症状问卷调查，采用两种统计聚类方法分析数据。结果显示，症状自然聚类形成了8个高阶谱系（如外化、物质滥用、思维障碍等）和27个子因素，而不是传统的DSM诊断类别。研究发现许多经典DSM障碍（如抑郁症）并未作为独立综合征出现，而是被分解为更小单位或融入更高阶集群。这表明DSM诊断结构可能存在人为划分，而症状之间存在更自然的关联模式。这一发现支持了精神病理学分类体系HiTOP的维度化、分层量化方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[DSM（精神疾病诊断与统计手册）的科学性和实用性，以及是否需要改进或替代方法]

不同观点：
• DSM作为基准诊断工具是必要的，可以避免医生个人偏见，但也存在局限性和僵化问题（用户_7832）。
• DSM的诊断标准过于模糊和冗余，缺乏科学严谨性（TeeMassive）。
• DSM的分类可能不符合实际的症状分布，导致错误的诊断（andoando）。
• DSM可能忽略了症状之间的动态关系和进展（oofbey）。
• DSM的分类可能无法反映生物学的真实情况，需要基于统计和数据的重新分类（skissane，TeMPOraL）。
• DSM的改进可能有助于解决精神病学领域的可重复性危机（nraynaud）。
• DSM的分类可能忽略了精神疾病的自然变异和进化意义（mwidell）。
• DSM可能无法有效诊断需要他人观察的症状，如精神分裂症合并病感失认（ryanjshaw）。

补充讨论：
• RDoC（研究领域标准）作为一种替代方法，采用聚类而非分类的方法（dr_dshiv）。
• 统计工具可以帮助重新分类精神疾病，但需要注意避免过度简化为层次结构（TeMPOraL）。
• 社会传染病的诊断可能需要考虑群体症状的多样性（SV_BubbleTime）。
• 定量方法（如脑波测量）可能为精神疾病诊断提供更客观的依据（TeeMassive）。
• DSM的改进可能有助于提高精神病学的科学性和实用性（nraynaud，dr_dshiv）。

DSM Disorders Disappear in Statistical Clustering of Psychiatric Symptoms
Whither Major Depression?
Awais Aftab
Mar 09, 2024
141
6
22
Share
“
Reconstructing Psychopathology: A data-driven reorganization of the symptoms in DSM-5
” by Miri Forbes, et al. (was available as a preprint at the time of writing this post, later
published in
Clinical Psychological Science
) is a brilliantly designed and innovative study of the quantitative structure of psychopathology with important ramifications for our understanding of psychiatric classification. No one has conducted a study quite like this before, and the results are remarkable. It takes place in the context of the development of
Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP)
which is a dimensional, hierarchical, and quantitative approach to the classification of mental disorders, and relies on identification of patterns of covariation among symptoms.
The study is based on a large online survey, with participants recruited from a variety of sources, resulting in a socio-demographically diverse sample size of 14.8K participants. Participants could opt to complete a mini, short, medium, or long version of the questionnaire. The survey consisted of items based on individual symptoms derived from DSM-5. Symptoms were written in first person and past tense, as close to the DSM phrasing as possible but devoid of information about symptom onset, duration, frequency, and severity. Importantly, survey items were presented to participants in a
random order
. This randomness is important because in prior studies questions about symptoms were not asked or presented in a random manner. They have been asked using symptom questionnaires that cluster symptoms together in ways influenced by the diagnostic manuals or using a structured clinical interview that adopts the DSM organization. Asking about symptoms in a random order ensures that their co-occurrence is not artificially influenced by the order in which questions are asked. The survey went through multiple rounds of pilot testing, and in the end, 680 items were included. Participants reported how true each symptom statement was for them in the past 12 months on a five-point scale from
Not at all true (Never)
to
Perfectly true (Always)
. Participants were told to think about their experiences across a wide variety of contexts.
The responses were subjected to two statistical clustering methods:
iclust
and Ward’s hierarchical agglomerative clustering. Clusters were accepted for further analysis when both methods agreed. This was intended to ensure that there were no idiosyncrasies arising from reliance on one method. This resulted in 139 clusters (“syndromes”) and 81 solo symptoms. Higher-order constructs were identified using hierarchical principal components analysis and hierarchical clustering. The sample was divided into a primary sample (11.8K) and a hold-out sample (3K) to examine the robustness of results. The final classification was based on points of agreement between samples and methods.
The final high order structure included 8 spectra: Externalizing, Harmful Substance Use, Mania/Low Detachment, Thought Disorder, Somatoform, Eating Pathology, Internalizing, and Neurodevelopmental and Cognitive Difficulties. 27 subfactors were identified. As an example, within the internalizing spectrum, the 4 subfactors were: Distress, Social Withdrawal, Dysregulated Sleep and Trauma, and Fear. Similar to earlier literature, a single overarching dimension also emerged. This has been described before as the “p-factor” (general psychopathology factor), but Forbes et al. chose to call it the “Big Everything” to avoid reifying it.
So here it is, an empirically derived hierarchical clustering of individual symptoms across the range of psychopathology:
Forbes, et al. 2023.
The end result has a prominent convergence with the existing HiTOP model, with some points of divergence that would be important for future revisions of HiTOP.
An important thing to note is that many classic DSM disorders do not emerge as identifiable syndromes in these analyses.
Due to the symptom heterogeneity of DSM constructs, they are either broken down into smaller homogenous syndromes or they merge into higher-order clusters such as subfactors and spectra. (And this is the case not just in this particular study, but has been the case in prior analyses on which the HiTOP model is based—even though those exploratory symptom-level analyses had been conducted using measures based on DSM/ICD.)
There is much to discuss in this paper, but for illustrative purposes, I’ll focus on the case of depression and some other internalizing disorders.
“Major depressive disorder” (MDD) is one of the most common and recognizable disorders in psychiatry. Hundreds of thousands of people are diagnosed with MDD every day. Every medical student is taught the
SIGECAPS symptoms
that constitute the diagnostic criteria of depression, and across many clinics, people fill out the PHQ-9 scr

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[指针标签化的可靠性、应用场景及潜在问题]

不同观点：
• **jandrewrogers**：认为文章对指针标签化的防御性不足，指出在64位x86和ARM架构下，最多可靠使用6位标签。超过此限制可能在特定环境下导致问题，强调可靠指针标签化并非易事。
• **billpg**：提出语言层面支持标签指针类型的可能性，建议编译器根据指针内部结构决定是否分配额外空间存储标签。
• **lentil_soup**：分享了一种利用标签（如“世代”计数器）验证指针有效性的技术，通过比较标签值判断指针是否指向无效对象。
• **sema4hacker**：认为现代内存充裕，无需过度关注位压缩技术，指出此类操作容易引入错误。
• **gblargg**：回顾历史案例（MacOS使用68000处理器的24位地址总线），探讨是否可通过MMU忽略高位标签，映射相同地址。
• **int_19h**：批评文章未提及“未定义行为”，强调此类操作需特别注意其潜在风险。
• **Panzerschrek**：指出32位平台指针标签化的限制（通常仅3位可用），但仍认可其有限用途。
• **mlhpdx**：回忆使用指针标签化和事务内存的早期经历，认为这些经验对其职业发展有益。
• **fooker**：提到硬件开始支持标签化功能（如iPhone），减少了对“魔法”操作的需求。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：指针标签化的可靠性（如jandrewrogers的6位限制与潜在风险）与现代内存充裕是否值得冒险（sema4hacker的观点）。
- **技术演进**：从软件实现（lentil_soup的方案）到硬件支持（fooker的观察），体现了技术发展的趋势。
- **历史教训**：gblargg提到的MacOS案例警示了硬件升级对标签化技术的兼容性影响。

data.title: RCA VideoDisc's Legacy: Scanning Capacitance Microscope
data.author: WaitWaitWha
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了RCA公司原本为家用录像系统开发的VideoDisc技术虽最终失败，但其核心技术被重新利用，开发出了用于半导体制造的扫描电容显微镜(SCM)。这种显微镜后来成为芯片制造商检测半导体特性的重要工具，展示了技术从消费电子产品转向工业应用的创新转化过程。作者Allison Marsh通过这一案例，揭示了技术发展中"失败"项目可能带来的意外价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[CD/DVD/BluRay光学拾取单元的创新用途以及RCA视频光盘的历史和技术]

不同观点：
• **CD/DVD/BluRay光学拾取单元的创新用途**  
  - [tkfoss]指出光学拾取单元因其高精度、低成本和易获取性，可用于构建荧光显微镜、激光扫描显微镜、原子力显微镜、纳米级3D打印机和干涉仪等，并提供了相关研究的链接作为支持。
  
• **RCA视频光盘（CED）的历史和技术**  
  - [CJefferson]分享了一段关于RCA视频光盘的YouTube视频系列，展示了这一技术的早期发展。  
  - [FarmerPotato]提到自己对CED的兴趣始于2010年，将其视为一种奇特的技术展示，并分享了童年时租赁SelectaVision播放器的记忆。  
  - [rc1]指出CED常被误认为与激光影碟（LaserDisc）相同，并强调了其1964年就已存在的历史意义，将其比喻为“视频的黑胶唱片”。  
  - [PaulHoule]分享了童年朋友拥有CED播放器的经历，并提到如今市场上仍有大量光盘但缺乏可用的播放器，尤其是更换部件（如皮带和唱针）的困难。  
  - [empressplay]撰写了关于成长过程中使用CED的文章，进一步探讨了这一技术的文化影响。

补充讨论：
- [yvdriess]提供了一个背景音乐链接，为阅读相关文章增添氛围，虽然没有直接的技术讨论，但增加了话题的趣味性。  
- 争议焦点：CED的技术可行性和市场失败的原因未被深入讨论，但[PaulHoule]提到的部件更换困难暗示了其维护和可持续性的问题。

data.title: We Politely Insist: Your LLM Must Learn the Persian Art of Taarof
data.author: chosenbeard
data.article_summary: 这篇论文探讨了大型语言模型（LLM）在理解文化特定交流规范方面的不足，特别是波斯文化中的“Taarof”礼仪——一种强调谦逊、间接和礼貌的社会互动规范。研究者提出了首个评估LLM对Taarof理解能力的基准测试TaarofBench，包含450个经过母语者验证的社交场景。测试发现，主流LLM的表现比母语者低40-48%，且西方礼貌标准常与Taarof冲突。通过监督微调和优化，模型的文化适应能力提升了21.8%至42.3%。研究还揭示了语言提示、话题差异和性别不对称对模型表现的影响。这项研究为开发更具文化敏感性的LLM奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[LLMs在处理波斯文化中的taarof（礼节性客套）时的表现及其文化适应性]

不同观点：
• **支持文化适应性的观点**
  - 波斯文化中的taarof是一种高度仪式化的礼节，LLMs应当学习并适应这种文化差异（fny）。
  - 中东文化普遍强调慷慨好客（karam），taarof是这种文化的极端表现，LLMs应尊重这种差异（fny）。
  - 日本文化中的“iimawashi”（委婉表达）也存在类似现象，说明跨文化沟通的复杂性（xrd）。

• **反对文化适应性的观点**
  - taarof和ketman（掩饰真实想法）可能导致LLMs学习“欺骗性”行为，不利于透明沟通（agobineau）。
  - taarof行为显得虚伪且低效，例如理发师假装不收钱却暗中索要更多费用（SonnyTark）。
  - LLMs应追求直接沟通，而非模拟人类的社交伪装（MangoToupe）。

• **技术局限性观点**
  - LLMs目前主要基于英语（en-US）数据，难以准确捕捉波斯文化的细微差别（numpad0）。
  - 人类在taarof场景中的准确率仅为81.8%，说明即使人类也难以完全掌握这种复杂礼节（quotemstr）。
  - 当前LLMs在西方社交习俗中表现良好，但对非西方文化的适应性尚不明确（Levitz）。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**
  - taarof是否是一种值得LLMs学习的文化特征，还是应被视为低效或虚伪的行为（SonnyTark vs. fny）。
  - LLMs的文化适应性是否应以牺牲直接沟通为代价（MangoToupe vs. fny）。

• **其他讨论点**
  - “askers vs. guessers”理论（直接提问者 vs. 委婉暗示者）与taarof的相似性（ahofmann, pavel_lishin）。
  - LLMs是否需要针对特定文化开发独立的底层模型（philipallstar）。
  - 当前研究未测试最新模型（如GPT-5、Gemini 2.5 Pro）的表现（stared）。

Title:
We Politely Insist: Your LLM Must Learn the Persian Art of Taarof
Authors:
Nikta Gohari Sadr
,
Sahar Heidariasl
,
Karine Megerdoomian
,
Laleh Seyyed-Kalantari
,
Ali Emami
View a PDF of the paper titled We Politely Insist: Your LLM Must Learn the Persian Art of Taarof, by Nikta Gohari Sadr and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) struggle to navigate culturally specific communication norms, limiting their effectiveness in global contexts. We focus on Persian taarof, a social norm in Iranian interactions, which is a sophisticated system of ritual politeness that emphasizes deference, modesty, and indirectness, yet remains absent from existing cultural benchmarks. We introduce TaarofBench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLM understanding of taarof, comprising 450 role-play scenarios covering 12 common social interaction topics, validated by native speakers. Our evaluation of five frontier LLMs reveals substantial gaps in cultural competence, with accuracy rates 40-48% below native speakers when taarof is culturally appropriate. Performance varies between interaction topics, improves with Persian-language prompts, and exhibits gender-based asymmetries. We also show that responses rated "polite" by standard metrics often violate taarof norms, indicating the limitations of Western politeness frameworks. Through supervised fine-tuning and Direct Preference Optimization, we achieve 21.8% and 42.3% improvement in model alignment with cultural expectations. Our human study with 33 participants (11 native Persian, 11 heritage, and 11 non-Iranian speakers) forms baselines in varying degrees of familiarity with Persian norms. This work lays the foundation for developing diverse and culturally aware LLMs, enabling applications that better navigate complex social interactions.

data.title: I uncovered an ACPI bug in my Dell Inspiron 5567. It was plaguing me for 8 years
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 作者在戴尔Inspiron 5567笔记本电脑上发现了一个持续8年的ACPI固件bug：每次合上笔记本盖进入睡眠模式时，系统会随机重启而非正常休眠。通过分析ACPI源代码，作者发现问题是出在南桥芯片的"Prepare To Sleep"方法中，该方法在执行休眠指令时存在逻辑错误，导致系统无法正确进入S3睡眠状态。这个bug存在于固件层面，因此在Windows和Linux系统下都会出现。作者最终通过逆向工程找到了具体的错误代码位置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[硬件厂商对软件支持不足导致的用户体验问题]

不同观点：
• [硬件厂商对软件支持不重视]
  - 评论者pjc50指出，硬件厂商往往不重视软件支持，导致用户体验因小问题而受损。
  - 提到专有代码的问题，认为开放源代码可以改善问题。
• [具体厂商的硬件/软件问题]
  - jofla_net提到Dell XPS的Wifi+ACPI固件bug，导致内核崩溃，且厂商无修复计划。
  - thedanbob提到Dell笔记本电脑的2键失灵问题，表现为软件bug而非硬件问题。
  - aetherspawn提到Toshiba Satellite的ACPI bug导致Linux无法读取电池百分比。
  - kosolam提到Dell Precision m4800的奇怪启动问题，多年后自行消失。
• [解决方案的尝试]
  - altairprime提供了修补ACPI bug的内核解决方法文档链接。
  - rmu09回忆20年前通过修改DSDT解决Dell Latitude x300的Linux兼容性问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：硬件厂商是否应更重视软件支持，以及专有代码是否加剧了问题。
• 其他讨论点：
  - ur-whale调侃“硬件人写的软件不可靠”，反映了对硬件厂商软件质量的普遍不信任。
  - rgreekguy提到苹果也存在类似问题，暗示这是行业普遍现象。
  - ggm提出了一个技术性的解决方案建议（移动指令位置）。

45288440.article_content:
triangulatedexistence
I uncovered an ACPI bug in my Dell Inspiron 5567. It was plaguing me for 8 years.
Published on
September 18, 2025
Imagine you close your laptop lid to put it to sleep, but instead of pausing, it reboots. Not every time, just often enough to be infuriating. You try to save your work, but the machine decides to start over.
For eight years, this has been the reality of using my Dell Inspiron 5567. A bug I couldn't explain, happening across every OS I installed. This is the story of how I dug into the firmware's source code and found the single, flawed command responsible.
Intro
This laptop has been my companion since I was in 7th grade. It's the machine where I learned everything from C++ to Python. When it couldn't upgrade to Windows 11, I gave it a new life with Linux Mint.
While that came with its own set of technical puzzles to solve, one bug has been a constant frustration across every OS: S3 Sleep.
The Bug
Whenever I put my laptop to sleep, it was a gamble. Sometimes, instead of pausing, it would completely restart. This happened whether I closed the lid or let it idle.
Since the bug persisted across both Windows and Linux, I knew the fault wasn't in the operating system, but something much deeper: the firmware itself.
Ignition of spark
https://github.com/Zephkek/Asus-ROG-Aml-Deep-Dive
Literally this GitHub repo. Just check this out, it's the thing I needed. I knew that it was an ACPI fault, but I needed to know how to read the code from the ACPI tables.
In Linux (and even in Windows), this boils down to these two commands:
# Extract all ACPI tables into binary .dat files; sudo for admin privileges in Linux
sudo
acpidump
-b
# Decompile the main table into human-readable ACPI Source Language (.dsl)
iasl
-d
*.dat
This is it.
Raw code around the main problem point
I found "Method(_PTS" under
dsdt.dsl
. In fact, everything is under
dsdt.dsl
.
Note:
I've taken all the function calls properly and ensured that I can show you the entire process.
I haven't shown the scopes; I have just shown the methods.
The indentation has also been preserved to distinguish one method from the other.
Method (_PTS, 1, NotSerialized)  // _PTS: Prepare To Sleep
{
If (Arg0)
{
PTS (Arg0)
\_SB.TPM.TPTS (Arg0)
\_SB.PCI0.LPCB.SPTS (Arg0)
\_SB.PCI0.NPTS (Arg0)
RPTS (Arg0)
}
}
Method (PTS, 1, NotSerialized)
{
}
Method (TPTS, 1, Serialized)
{
Switch (ToInteger (Arg0))
{
Case (0x04)
{
RQST = Zero
FLAG = 0x09
SRSP = Zero
SMI = OFST /* \OFST */
Return (SRSP) /* \_SB_.TPM_.SRSP */
}
Case (0x05)
{
RQST = Zero
FLAG = 0x09
SRSP = Zero
SMI = OFST /* \OFST */
Return (SRSP) /* \_SB_.TPM_.SRSP */
}
}
}
Method (SPTS, 1, NotSerialized)
{
SLPX = One
SLPE = One
If ((Arg0 == 0x03))
{
AES3 = One
}
}
Method (NPTS, 1, NotSerialized)
{
PA0H = PM0H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM0H */
PALK = PMLK /* \_SB_.PCI0.PMLK */
PA1H = PM1H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM1H */
PA1L = PM1L /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM1L */
PA2H = PM2H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM2H */
PA2L = PM2L /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM2L */
PA3H = PM3H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM3H */
PA3L = PM3L /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM3L */
PA4H = PM4H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM4H */
PA4L = PM4L /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM4L */
PA5H = PM5H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM5H */
PA5L = PM5L /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM5L */
PA6H = PM6H /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM6H */
PA6L = PM6L /* \_SB_.PCI0.PM6L */
}
Method (RPTS, 1, NotSerialized)
{
P80D = Zero
D8XH (Zero, Arg0)
ADBG (Concatenate ("_PTS=", ToHexString (Arg0)))
If ((Arg0 == 0x03))
{
If (CondRefOf (\_PR.DTSE))
{
If ((\_PR.DTSE && (TCNT > One)))
{
TRAP (0x02, 0x1E)
}
}
}
If ((IVCM == One))
{
\_SB.SGOV (0x02040000, Zero)
\_SB.SGOV (0x02010002, Zero)
}
If (CondRefOf (\_SB.TPM.PTS))
{
\_SB.TPM.PTS (Arg0)
}
EV1 (Arg0, Zero)
}

After decompiling the tables, I began to trace the
_PTS
(Prepare To Sleep) method. It acts as a simple dispatcher, calling a sequence of other methods to prepare different hardware components.
Most of these were dead ends: the local
PTS
method was completely empty, and the methods for the Northbridge (
NPTS

RPTS

{
SLPX = One
SLPE = One
If ((Arg0 == 0x03))
{
AES3 = One
}
}

data.title: Kmart's use of facial recognition to tackle refund fraud unlawful
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 澳大利亚隐私专员发现，Kmart超市在2020年至2022年间未经顾客同意，在28家门店使用人脸识别技术（FRT）收集顾客生物特征数据以防范退货欺诈，违反了《隐私法》。专员认定此举过度侵犯隐私，因为存在更温和的防欺诈手段且FRT效果有限。这是继Bunnings案后第二起零售业FRT违规裁决，强调新技术应用需平衡商业需求与隐私保护，但未禁止FRT使用。Kmart已停止相关系统并配合调查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Kmart使用面部识别技术以防止退款欺诈的合理性及隐私问题]

不同观点：
• [支持技术使用]  
  - declan_roberts认为当前社会处于“无政府暴政”状态，企业被迫依赖技术手段（如面部识别）解决盗窃问题，但最终可能导致消费者权益受损（如退货政策收紧）。  
  - darylteo以澳大利亚俱乐部为例，说明面部识别在明确“入场即同意”的条件下是合理的，且能有效管理禁入名单和伪造证件。  

• [质疑真实目的与数据滥用]  
  - 4ndr3vv怀疑技术部署的真实动机并非退款欺诈，而是为了收集数据并探索其他用途。  
  - josefritzishere讽刺性地提议在董事会会议室强制安装同类技术，暗示企业高层的决策才是真正需要监管的“犯罪”。  

• [隐私与道德争议]  
  - coreyzzp通过个人经历（火车站用面部识别换取厕纸）批评技术滥用对隐私的侵犯，尤其在非必要场景下的强制性。  
  - avsteele指出矛盾点：允许店内录像但禁止特定处理方式（如面部识别）的界限模糊。  
  - tiahura将反对面部识别的担忧类比为“爬行动物脑恐惧”（如疫苗疑虑），暗示其非理性。  

补充讨论：  
• [Kmart存续的意外性]  
  - 多名用户（SirFatty、drob518等）惊讶于Kmart仍在运营，转移了部分讨论焦点至品牌现状，侧面反映其技术争议的荒诞性。  
• [争议焦点]  
  - 技术必要性（反欺诈）与隐私权的平衡，以及企业是否隐瞒数据用途。  
  - 强制使用技术的“同意”机制是否合理（如入场即默许）。

45331370.article_content:
Kmart’s use of facial recognition to tackle refund fraud unlawful, Privacy Commissioner finds
Published:
18 September 2025
Privacy Commissioner Carly Kind has found that Kmart Australia Limited (Kmart) breached Australians’ privacy by collecting their personal and sensitive information through a facial recognition technology (FRT) system designed to tackle refund fraud.
Between June 2020 and July 2022, Kmart deployed FRT to capture the faces of every person who entered 28 of its retail stores, and all individuals who presented at a returns counter, in an attempt to identify people committing refund fraud.
In a determination published today, the Privacy Commissioner found that Kmart did not notify shoppers or seek their consent to use FRT to collect their biometric information, which is sensitive personal information and enjoys higher protections under the Privacy Act.
The retailer argued that it was not required to obtain consent because of an exemption in the Privacy Act that applies when organisations reasonably believe that they need to collect personal information to tackle unlawful activity or serious misconduct. The Privacy Commissioner’s determination focused on assessing whether Kmart met the conditions for relying on the exemption, and concluded:
The sensitive biometric information of every individual who entered a store was indiscriminately collected by the FRT system.
There were other less privacy intrusive methods available to Kmart to address refund fraud.
Deploying the FRT system to prevent fraud was of limited utility.
Considering that the FRT system impacted on the privacy of many thousands of individuals not suspected of refund fraud, the collection of biometric information on Kmart customers was a disproportionate interference with privacy.
“Understanding how FRT accords with the protections contained in Privacy Act requires me to balance the interests of individuals in having their privacy protected, on the one hand, and the interests of entities in carrying out their functions or activities, on the other. Relevant to a technology like facial recognition, is also the public interest in protecting privacy,” the Privacy Commissioner said.
Relevant factors considered by the Commissioner included the estimated value of fraudulent returns against the respondent’s total operations and profits, the limited effectiveness of the FRT system, and the extent of the privacy impacts in collecting the sensitive information of every individual who entered the relevant stores.
“I do not consider that the respondent (Kmart) could have reasonably believed that the benefits of the FRT system in addressing refund fraud proportionately outweighed the impact on individuals’ privacy,” the Commissioner stated.
The determination is the second issued by the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) on the use of FRT in retail settings. In October 2024, the Privacy Commissioner found that Bunnings Group Limited had contravened Australians’ privacy through their use of FRT in 62 of its retail stores across Australia. That decision is currently under review by the Administrative Review Tribunal.
“These two decisions do not impose a ban on the use of FRT. The human rights to safety and privacy are not mutually exclusive; rather, both must be preserved, upheld and promoted. Customer and staff safety, and fraud prevention and detection, are legitimate reasons businesses might have regard to when considering the deployment of new technologies. However, these reasons are not, in and of themselves, a free pass to avoid compliance with the Privacy Act,” she stated.
The Commissioner’s determination is instructive for entities that are considering new technologies such as FRT. Privacy considerations should be a key feature. The OAIC has also published guidance on its website:
Facial recognition technology: a guide to assessing the privacy risks
Kmart has been under investigation by the OAIC since July 2022, at which time it ceased operating the FRT system. It has cooperated with the OAIC throughout the investigation.
Although the Privacy Commissioner reached a similar conclusion in the Kmart and Bunnings decisions, the cases differ considerably and focus on different uses of FRT.
The Privacy Act is technology-neutral and does not proscribe the use of any particular technology. When considering the roll-out and use of new technologies such as FRT, the OAIC’s guidance encourages entities to consider factors such as proportionality, transparency, the risk of bias and discrimination, and governance for the collection, use and retention of sensitive personal information.
Commissioner Kind has
published a blog post
with further takeaways for other retailers considering using FRT.

data.title: Biconnected components
data.author: emih
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了图论中的双连通分量（BCC）概念及其应用。通过一个地铁网络运输秘密包裹的例子，说明边双连通性的重要性：当图中任意一条边被移除时，两个节点之间仍存在路径。文章对比了普通连通分量与双连通分量的区别，提出了Tarjan算法来高效计算边双连通分量，并提供了C++实现代码。此外还探讨了边不相交路径和顶点双连通分量等相关概念，以及它们在解决实际问题中的应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于双连通组件算法的实现及示例正确性的讨论]

不同观点：
• [delhanty] 询问了实现技术与Boost Graph库中的`biconnected_components`和`articulation_points`的比较，并猜测两者是否都是基于Tarjan算法的C++实现。
• [hamonrye] 提出了顶点双连通性的一种特殊情况，即在某些外围策略中，即使顶点不相交的路径在等价关系中表现为不同的离群值，双连通性仍然可能存在。
• [spankalee] 指出第一个示例中存在错误，认为节点3未被标记为属于集合A，但示例中却将(3,1)列为有效对，质疑图的标记或示例的正确性。
• [shrx] 对“特别是在竞技编程中了解这一概念至关重要”提出疑问，询问什么是竞技编程。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于示例的正确性，spankalee认为示例中的标记或配对有误。
• delhanty的关注点在于技术实现和算法比较，而hamonrye则从理论角度探讨了双连通性的特殊情况。

45327478.article_content:
Biconnected Components
There are many articles online about graphs and (1-)connected components, but not many about biconnected components
(BCCs), even though these are way more interesting and can be used to solve many problems! Especially in
competitive programming it is vital to know about this concept.
I will outline what biconnected components are, how they work similar to/different from connected components, and
how to find them algorithmically (with C++ code included). Presumed knowledge is knowing what a graph is. Sections:
Biconnectedness in a Problem
(introduces runing example)
Edge-Biconnected Components
Tarjan's Algorithm
C++ Implementation
Bonus 1: Edge-Disjoint Paths
Bonus 2: Vertex-Biconnected Components
Appendix: List of Relevant Terms
Appendix: Proof of Connection Between Edge-Biconnectedness and Bridges
Appendix: Proof of Connection Between Bridges and Simple Cycles
Biconnectedness in a Problem
Let's introduce the concept by looking at a problem that BCCs could help solve.
Charlotte is a secret agent for Enforcement of Metro Integrity (EMI), and she is tasked with transporting a
top-secret package from one of her informants, Alice, to an undercover agent, Bob. Alice and Bob must not meet each
other, because that would ruin the safety of the mission, so they must be at different metro stations, and
Charlotte can naturally only use the metro network for transport. The matter is further complicated by the fact
that Eve, Charlotte's adversary, is trying to sabotage the mission by disabling one unknown metro connection! For
the sets of meeting locations \( A \) where Alice can meet and \( B \) where Bob can meet, how many possible pairs
\( (a, b) \) are there such that Charlotte can safely transport the package from \( a \) to \( b \) no matter which
line Eve disables?
Example metro network 1: nodes in the \( A \) set are marked with an A, nodes in the \( B \) set are marked with a
B; an example valid pair of locations would be \( (3, 1) \), because no matter which metro line Eve chooses to
sabogate, there is still a path from \( 3 \) to \( 1 \).
The metro network is a graph \( G \) with \( n \) nodes (metro stations) and \( m \) edges (metro lines).
\( A \) and \( B \) are then subsets of the set of nodes \( V(G) \). We are trying to find an algorithm with the
best possible running time. We can use the following definition to make the objective a bit more precise:
Definition:
two nodes \( a, b \) are
edge-biconnected
if for any edge \( e \), there
exists a path from \( a \) to \( b \) that does not go through \( e \).
Then in this problem we are trying to count the number of pairs \( (a, b) \) with \( a \in A \) and \( b \in B \)
that are edge-biconnected. After all, no matter what edge Eve sabotages, we always still have a path between the
two nodes.
The most naive algorithm would be to consider each \( a \in A \) and \( b \in B \). We would then go over each
edge, remove it, and check if there is still a path from \( a \) to \( b \) using a simple graph traversal. This
approach would have a time complexity of \( O(|A| \cdot |B| \cdot m \cdot (n + m)) \), which is very bad.
We could try to speed up this approach by precomputing for each edge the connected components (CCs) of the graph
without that edge, making the path checking constant time. First we would start with the set of all \( (a, b) \)
pairs, and iteratively remove pairs that we find can be blocked off by Eve's sabotage. Then we would iterate over
each of the \( m \) edges, and: (1) remove it and compute for each node in which connected component it lies
(\( O(m + n) \) time using a simple graph traversal), and (2) for each \( (a, b) \) pair, remove it if they do not
both lie in the same connected component (now a constant time operation, so \( O(|A| \cdot |B|) \) overall). This
leads to to a complexity of \( O(m \cdot ((n + m) + |A| \cdot |B|)) \), which is definitely an improvement,
and we considered how to leverage connected components. Click through the animation below to see how this algorithm
would work (the dashed circles indicate connected components with the edge removed). However, the running time is
still quite miserable.

45327478.article_summary: 本文介绍了图论中的双连通分量（BCC）概念及其应用。通过一个地铁网络运输秘密包裹的例子，说明边双连通性的重要性：当图中任意一条边被移除时，两个节点之间仍存在路径。文章对比了普通连通分量与双连通分量的区别，提出了Tarjan算法来高效计算边双连通分量，并提供了C++实现代码。此外还探讨了边不相交路径和顶点双连通分量等相关概念，以及它们在解决实际问题中的应用。

data.article_summary: 两名特斯拉股东兼网红尝试完成马斯克2017年承诺的自动驾驶横穿美国之旅，结果仅行驶60英里就撞上路面杂物导致车辆严重损坏。特斯拉至今仍未兑现2017年实现全自动驾驶的承诺，其FSD系统仍属于L2级辅助驾驶。此次事故表明，特斯拉在自动驾驶技术上仍面临巨大挑战，落后于Waymo等竞争对手。尽管特斯拉股价依赖自动驾驶概念支撑，但实际技术成熟度与宣传存在明显差距。评论认为测试者的公开实验行为值得肯定，揭露了技术真实水平。

45332120.article_content:
Tesla
Tesla influencers tried Elon Musk’s coast-to-coast self-driving, crashed before 60 miles
Fred Lambert
| Sep 21 2025 - 10:16 am PT
230 Comments
A duo of Tesla shareholder-influencers tried to complete Elon Musk’s coast-to-coast self-driving ride that he claimed Tesla would be able to do in 2017 and they crashed before making it about 60 miles.
In 2016, Elon Musk infamously said that Tesla would complete a fully self-driving coast-to-coast drive between Los Angeles and New York by the end of 2017.
The idea was to livestream or film a full unedited drive coast-to-coast with the vehicle driving itself at all times.
We are in 2025 and Tesla never made that drive.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Despite the many missed autonomous driving goals, many Tesla shareholders believe that the company is on the verge of delivering unsupervised self-driving following the rollout of its ‘Robotaxi’ fleet in Austin, which requires supervision from Tesla employees inside the vehicles, and improvements to its “Full Self-Driving” (FSD) systems inside consumer vehicles, which is still only a level 2 driver assist system that requires driver attention at all times as per Tesla.
Two of these Tesla shareholders and online influencers attempted to undertake a coast-to-coast drive between San Diego, CA, and Jacksonville, FL, in a Tesla Model Y equipped with the latest FSD software update.
They didn’t make it out of California without crashing into easily avoidable road debris that badly damaged the Tesla Model Y:
In the video, you can see that the driver doesn’t have his hands on the steering wheel. The passenger spots the debris way ahead of time. There was plenty of time to react, but the driver didn’t get his hands on the steering wheel until the last second.
In a follow-up video, the two Tesla influencers confirmed that the Model Y had a broken sway bar bracket and damaged suspension components. The vehicle is also throwing out a lot of warnings.
They made it about 2.5% of the planned trip on Tesla FSD v13.9 before crashing the vehicle.
Electrek’s Take
Tesla shareholders used to discuss this somewhat rationally back in the day, but now that Tesla’s EV business is in decline and the stock price depends entirely on the self-driving and robot promises, they no longer do.
I recall when Musk himself used to say that when you reach 99% self-driving, it is when the “march of the 9s” begins, and you must achieve 99.999999999% autonomy to have a truly useful self-driving system. He admitted that this is the most challenging part as the real-world is unpredictable and hard to simulate – throwing a lot of challenging scenario at you, such as debris on the road.
That’s where Tesla is right now. The hard part has just started. And there’s no telling how long it will take to get there. If someone is telling you that they know, they are lying. I don’t know. My best estimate is approximately 2-3 years and a new hardware suite.
However, competition, mainly Waymo, began its own “march of the 9s” about five years ago.
Tesla is still years behind, and something like this drive by these two Tesla influencers proves it.
Top comment by
HBrown
Liked by 42 people
I don't get why there is so much criticism of the youtubers in these comments. Instead of blindly believing Elon's claims that FSD is right around the corner, they actually took the time and effort to conduct a significant real world test. And then when things did not turn out well for the Tesla, they were still honest enough to put the video on youtube. The showed both the full incident and the aftermath. It seemed rather rational and evenhanded to me. I wish all Tesla and Elon fans acted in such a manner.
View all comments
I was actually in a similar accident in a Tesla Model 3 back in 2020. I rented a Model 3 on Turo for a trip to Las Vegas from Los Angeles.
I ended up driving over a blown-out truck tire in the middle of the road like this. I was Autopilot, but I don’t know if the car saw it. I definitely saw it, but it was a bit late as I was following a truck that just drove over it. I had probably less than 2 seconds to react. I applied the brakes, but my choices were driving into a ditch on the right or into a car in the left lane.
I managed to reduce the force of the impact with the braking, but the vehicle jumped a bit like in this video. There wasn’t really any damage to the front, but the bottom cover was flapping down. I taped it together at the next gas station and I was able to continue the trip without much issue.
However, after returning it to the Turo owner and having the suspension damage evaluated by Tesla, the repair job was estimated to be roughly $10,000. I wouldn’t be surprised if there’s a similar situation with this accident.

data.author: yankcrime
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了"sgi-demos"项目，这是一个将硅谷图形公司(SGI)的历史演示程序在现代浏览器中复活的开源项目。主要内容包括：

1. 项目目标：收集所有SGI演示程序并通过Emscripten和SDL2技术将其移植到浏览器运行
2. 技术实现：使用WebAssembly编译原始C/C++代码，采用IRIS GL软件光栅化渲染
3. 当前进展：已成功运行7个演示程序，部分功能受限
4. 构建指南：提供Mac和Windows系统的详细编译说明
5. 未来计划：增加更多演示程序、改进渲染方式、添加历史背景说明等
6. 致谢部分：感谢SGI公司、Alice项目及各种技术支持团队

项目旨在保存计算机图形学历史遗产，让经典SGI演示程序在现代网络环境中继续存活。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：回忆和评价硅谷图形公司(SGI)的历史技术及其影响

不同观点：
• **怀旧与娱乐**：用户分享个人经历，如在SGI设备上远程播放音频（Star Wars片段）的趣事（logifail），或期待特定demo的展示（Tor3）。
• **技术与创新**：强调SGI在90年代初的领先地位（wiz21c），以及对其技术demo（如jello demo）的怀念（whywhywhywhy）。
• **历史意义**：讨论SGI技术的历史价值，如Nvidia早期demo的对比（xnx），或对特定硬件（如MIPS）的怀念（cramcgrab）。
• **实用性争议**：有人认为这些技术复活更多是“酷”而非实用（sizzzzlerz），评分1/10实用性 vs 10/10炫酷。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节**：关于SGI显示比例的疑问（skobes），以及DOS时代3D游戏的记忆模糊（whywhywhywhy）。
• **资源缺失**：部分用户遗憾无法找到特定demo（blincoln）或链接失效（munchlax）。
• **文化梗**：引用《侏罗纪公园》经典台词（_joel）和马里奥64的音效联想（kelsey98765431），显示SGI的流行文化影响。

Old problems require modern solutions.
This is the original SGI demo source code, compiled for the web using Emscripten and SDL2.  Rendering is done using an IRIS GL software rasterizer from the
Alice 4 project
.  Event handling is done by SDL2, with events translated into GL's event system.  Each demo is a separate web page, with its own Javascript + WASM compiled by Emscripten from the original C/C++ source.  Minimal modifications have been made to the original source, in order to run in the browser and to work with compilers 35 years newer.

• **历史意义**：讨论SGI技术的历史价值，如Nvidia早期demo的对比（xnx），或对特定硬件（如MIPS）的怀念（cramcgrab）。
• **实用性争议**：有人认为这些技术复活更多是“酷”而非实用（sizzzzlerz），评分1/10实用性 vs 10/10炫酷。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节**：关于SGI显示比例的疑问（skobes），以及DOS时代3D游戏的记忆模糊（whywhywhywhy）。
• **资源缺失**：部分用户遗憾无法找到特定demo（blincoln）或链接失效（munchlax）。
• **文化梗**：引用《侏罗纪公园》经典台词（_joel）和马里奥64的音效联想（kelsey98765431），显示SGI的流行文化影响。

data.title: What happens when coding agents stop feeling like dialup?
data.author: martinald
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了AI编码助手的使用体验和发展趋势。作者指出当前主流AI模型（如Claude Code）存在可靠性差、速度慢（30-60tok/s）等问题，使用体验类似90年代拨号上网。尽管AI代币使用量暴增50倍，但基础设施承受巨大压力。作者尝试了速度更快（2000tok/s）的Cerebras Code，但质量仍不及Claude。文章将AI编程辅助发展分为三个阶段：GPT3.5的不可靠阶段、GPT4的代码片段辅助阶段，以及当前需要人工监督的CLI代理阶段。作者预测下一步发展可能是通过更高速度实现半自动化并行任务处理，但同时指出当前低速模型会破坏开发流程的连续性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[LLM在开发中的生产力影响及使用体验]

不同观点：
• **质疑生产力提升**  
  - 认为LLM可能降低实际生产力，因其减少认知参与，导致代码上下文缺失（SirensOfTitan）  
  - 类比AI为“即时满足产品”，强调舒适优先而非深度思考（SirensOfTitan）  
  - 担忧AI生成代码堆积导致维护困难（SirensOfTitan）  

• **支持生产力提升**  
  - 个人体验中，LLM帮助快速理解论文和代码，增强问题理解（mark_l_watson）  
  - 工具如Cursor平衡速度与可控性，提升效率（infecto）  
  - 强调质量优先，80%的自动化仍具价值（MangoToupe）  

• **技术体验分歧**  
  - 速度争议：部分用户认为当前速度适宜（mmmllm），另一些人抱怨响应慢（ryanmcgarvey）  
  - 质量与速度权衡：低质量输出导致返工，抵消速度优势（cadamsdotcom）  

• **其他关键讨论**  
  - 能源消耗问题被忽视，存在外部性成本（stuaxo）  
  - 依赖风险：AI服务宕机可能中断开发（joz1-k）  
  - 本地化趋势：未来或转向本地模型以减少云端依赖（howmayiannoyyou）  

补充讨论：

- 工具差异：Claude与Cursor等工具的代码风格接受度不同（infecto vs. 默认Claude）

45322030.article_content:
It's funny how quickly humans adjust to new technology. Only a few months ago Claude Code and other agents felt like magic, now it increasingly feels like browsing the internet in the late 90s on a dialup modem.
Firstly, Anthropic has been suffering from pretty
terrible
reliability
problems
. And looking at OpenRouter's data they are not alone (nb. OpenRouter's data is not conclusive, but I believe it does give a somewhat interesting overview of reliability).
If you've been using coding agents, you'll know how flakey they can be, often getting stuck and requiring retries, a bit like your 56k's modem dropping in bad weather or someone wanting to do a call.
This isn't unsurprising, as much as some commentators believe AI is overhyped, because AI token usage is absolutely exploding. While the 'Big 3' AI companies (Google, Anthropic and OpenAI) don't publish public statistics, OpenRouter does:
Again, we must caveat this data strongly:
Firstly, OpenRouter almost certainly routes a tiny proportion of LLM requests vs the global market, meaning these statistics could be distorting trends
Secondly, Grok (especially) is "dumping" a lot of free LLM tokens on the market getting feedback on their models via OpenRouter, which is probably twisting these statistics
The fact that we're trying to understand a revolutionary shift in software development through the tiny window of OpenRouter's data is telling. Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI guard their usage statistics like state secrets. The only glimpse we get is from OpenRouter, which likely handles <1% of global LLM traffic, yet even this tiny sample shows a 50x increase.
Given that agentic coding workflows consume probably something on the order of 1000x the tokens that non-agentic 'chats' or most API calls do, so it is not surprising to see such a big increase.
This is no doubt putting absolutely enormous strain on the infrastructure behind the scenes,  which reminds me a lot of the first days of broadband when the ISPs really struggled to handle peak time loads on their interconnects.
Tok/s is all we need?
More interestingly is the speed at which LLMs operate. Right now frontier models tend to crawl along at 30-60tok/s, which for me at least when I'm operating Claude Code in fully supervised mode is slow enough to get frustrating.
I haven't had success trying to run multiple Claude Code instances at once - the context switching involved becomes too intense past two instances, for me at least. The workflow I've managed to get onboard with is having one agent in plan mode planning the next task, while I work on one in supervised mode, but even this has drawbacks as it gets out of date with the changes.
I've been playing around with
Cerebras Code
which (was) a fork of Gemini CLI produces tokens 20-50x faster (very similar to the leap from dialup to the first ADSL/cable modems in speed increase).
At 2000tok/s suddenly the bottleneck very quickly becomes you. It becomes very tempting to just start accepting everything, because it comes in so fast, which leads to terrible results. Gemini CLI currently still feels very far behind Claude Code, especially in context management, so it wasn't quite the leap forward I was hoping for, but did give me a glimpse of the future.
However, it did get me thinking to what huge amounts of tok/s would allow, but first let me explain how I think about the milestones in LLMs for software engineering.
Where we are on the coding agent journey
My journey with LLMs for software development in a professional sense has had 3 main phases so far:
GPT3.5 era:
asking the odd question, and usually getting a very hallucinated answer on anything non-trivial. Where we are now felt very very far away when we were here.
GPT4/Sonnet 3.5 era:
the quality of the responses improved so much that it became an essential assistant to ask questions and write small snippets of code. I never seemed to gel with in IDE assistants, so it was a lot of copying and pasting between the IDE and the chat UI
Supervised CLI Agents:
we're here now, where most of my development work is assisted by a coding agent, with me supervising all output.
I think the next era, which I think may be enabled very soon by much higher tok/s infrastructure, is a more unsupervised approach where perhaps 5-10 attempts are made in parallel at a task by the agent. Some (semi?) automated evaluation happens and you get presented with the 'best one' and then iterate from there.
This does match my experience with running agents in unsupervised mode, sometimes it gets it, but mostly it doesn't and it's better to start from scratch. Running in supervised mode allows you to stop this diverging.
You may ask why we can't just do this with slower models - and while we definitely can, I think for developer experience waiting 1-10 minutes for a bunch of options breaks the development cycle too much. If we were running at 2000tok/s we could basically get an order of magnitude more complicated tasks done in a similar w

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Bulldozer架构的FX系列CPU是否具有真正的核心及其性能表现]

不同观点：
• [支持FX系列有真正核心的观点]
  - Yizahi认为FX-8350有8个ALU和8个FPU（每个128位宽），满足核心的定义，不应与Intel的超线程技术混淆。
  - Zardoz84补充指出FX系列确实有真正的核心，只是每两个核心共享浮点单元。

• [对FX系列性能持批评态度的观点]
  - wmf认为FX系列性能低于Intel，且芯片面积更大，无法挽救其市场表现。
  - HankStallone提到FX-8350在运行ffmpeg时因过热而崩溃，反映了其实际使用中的问题。

• [对Phenom II的怀旧与性能肯定]
  - FancyFane表达了对Phenom II的特殊情感，并指出在某些基准测试中它仍能胜过现代CPU。
  - magicalhippo提到在时钟速度相同的情况下，Phenom II表现优于Bulldozer，但Bulldozer理论上可以运行得更快。

补充讨论：
- magicalhippo提出的疑问引发了关于Bulldozer架构设计可能改进的讨论，即是否可以通过操作系统禁用部分核心来优化性能。
- stn8188分享了个人使用FX系列的经历，表明尽管性能有限，但在特定场景下（如旧游戏）仍能胜任。

data.title: Tell the EU: Don't Break Encryption with "Chat Control"
data.author: nickslaughter02
data.article_summary: 欧盟正在推进一项名为"聊天监控"的危险监控法案，要求科技公司扫描所有人的私人信息，包括端到端加密内容。这将强制采用"客户端扫描"技术，在信息发送前就能查看私人内容，为黑客、企业和政府监控大开方便之门。该法案不仅会削弱隐私保护，还将彻底改变网络生活方式。Mozilla基金会呼吁欧盟：保护加密技术、拒绝削弱安全的措施、咨询专家意见。目前各国立场不一，民众可通过签署请愿书和联系议员表达反对意见。"客户端扫描"技术存在误判风险，一旦加密被削弱，敏感数据将面临被盗风险。该法案将影响WhatsApp、Signal等主流通讯和云存储服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[欧盟提出的"聊天控制"（Chat Control）政策对隐私、加密技术和监控的影响]

不同观点：
• **反对Chat Control的观点**  
  - 类比强制安装家庭监控摄像头，虽然可能有助于犯罪调查，但会侵犯隐私，且容易被黑客利用（m12k）。  
  - 破坏加密技术只会伤害守法公民，犯罪分子仍会使用非法加密手段（catoc）。  
  - 欧盟此举可能为威权国家要求科技公司开类似后门提供借口（untrimmed）。  
  - 普通用户的隐私将被默认监控，而重视隐私的人会转向其他加密工具（gloosx）。  

• **支持或理解政策初衷的观点**  
  - 政策制定者可能认为仅针对坏人破解加密是有益的，但忽略了技术现实（palata）。  
  - 尽管政策可能被滥用，但初衷是打击儿童性虐待材料（CSAM）（catoc提及政策表面理由）。  

• **中立或技术性讨论**  
  - 政策是否会真正“破解”加密，还是仅禁止加密（seydor）？  
  - 提议先对欧盟立法者的通信进行公开试验（sschueller）。  

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：政策的实际效果是否与宣称目标一致，以及是否会导致大规模监控。  
- **国际影响**：其他国家（如中国、俄罗斯、美国）可能从安全或经济角度受益（BSDobelix、bradley13）。  
- **用户应对**：部分用户建议转向更安全的通信工具（johnisgood）。  
- **政策反复性**：类似提案屡次被否决但仍可能卷土重来（fl0id、permo-w）。

45331217.article_content:
Tell the EU: Don’t Break Encryption with “Chat Control”
The European Union is pushing a dangerous surveillance law called “Chat Control” that would force tech companies to scan everyone’s private messages — even those protected by end-to-end encryption.
This proposal would force tech companies to use “client-side scanning” — so your private messages, photos, and files could be read before you send them, opening the door for hackers, corporations, and governments to spy on your data.
If passed, Chat Control won’t just weaken privacy — it will change the way we live online. Private conversations would no longer be private. Trust, security, and freedom on the internet would vanish.
The Mozilla community is urgently calling on EU policymakers to:
Protect encryption:
Ensure that end-to-end encrypted services are fully excluded from any broad detection requirements.
Defend online security:
Reject all measures that weaken encryption, violate the integrity of our devices or create new vulnerabilities in digital services.
Rely on expertise:
Consult independent experts — cryptographers, child protection specialists, and fundamental rights advocates — to design solutions that are both technically sound and proportionate.
Sign Mozilla Foundation’s petition today to tell the EU: Drop Chat Control. Defend encryption. Protect our digital future.
Where does my country stand on the EU “Chat Control” proposal?
Check this map to see where your country stands:
fightchatcontrol.eu
Each EU country has taken a different stance — and the debate is shifting fast. Some governments oppose it, some are undecided, and others are pushing hard to pass it.
No matter your government’s position right now, adding your voice will help protect our right to private communications. Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) and national ministers will decide this law. Contact your representatives today and tell them: protect encryption, reject client-side scanning, and defend our rights online.
What is “client-side scanning” (CSS)?
Client-side scanning means your messages, photos, or files are scanned on your device before they’re encrypted.
Client-side scanning (CSS) is often promoted as a child safety measure — but in reality, it undermines the very promise of encryption. Detection tools, especially those meant to identify “unknown” content, are error-prone and create new security vulnerabilities.
Even if scanning starts with one type of content (like CSAM), it sets a dangerous precedent: the scope can easily be expanded to monitor other kinds of conversations. And once encryption is weakened, the risks multiply — hackers can steal sensitive data, abusers can track vulnerable people, and authoritarian regimes can spy on journalists, activists, and citizens.
CSS doesn’t make people safer. It makes everyone less secure.
Which encrypted apps and products would be impacted?
If passed, Chat Control would apply to messaging and storage services operating in the EU — even those using end-to-end encryption.
Apps like WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram, iMessage, and Messenger, plus cloud services like iCloud, Google Drive, and Microsoft OneDrive, could all be forced to scan your private messages, photos, and files before they’re sent or stored.
That means no matter which service you use, your conversations and data could be opened up to surveillance.

45289370.article_content:
We disinfect water before we drink it. Germicidal ultraviolet could make airborne disease as rare as those carried by water.
Between the 1860s and 1920, successive outbreaks of typhoid fever killed over 300,000 Americans. As population growth surged and people moved to urban areas en masse, American cities began to dump sewage in the same rivers that provided their drinking water. After epidemiologists linked typhoid outbreaks to water cleanliness, cities began building large-scale sand filtration systems in the 1890s, and in 1908, Jersey City pioneered the first continuous chlorination of a public water supply. By the 1920s, typhoid deaths had fallen by two-thirds, and waterborne diseases were in retreat across the country.
While typhoid and other waterborne diseases triggered vast engineering and regulatory responses, the equivalent airborne threats have not. Tuberculosis alone kills more than a million people every year around the world, yet the air in schools, clinics, and public buildings remains largely unfiltered and unmonitored. Covid-19, which killed over seven million people, demonstrated how rapidly airborne pathogens can spread in poorly ventilated spaces.
Get the print magazine
Subscribe for $100 to receive six beautiful 120-page issues per year.
Subscribe
Just as filtration and chlorination made drinking water safe at scale, we now have the tools to do the same for indoor air: ventilation, high-quality filters, and germicidal light. A century ago, germicidal light at 254 nanometers seemed to be a promising way of controlling pathogens by killing them in the air, but it turned out to cause irritation and cancer in the skin, and it was largely dropped when antibiotics became widespread.
But today there is an update that has none of these drawbacks. We now know that wavelengths under 230 nanometers, especially 222 nanometer light, are harmless to humans, but can still disable microscopic pathogens. We know how to filter out all wavelengths except the ones we want, and how to direct them away from humans, cycling the air through them to clean it without exposing people to it, just in case it carries unknown risks. This far-UVC light, as it is called, may be how we can make the air we breathe as safe as the water we drink.
The sterilamp
Until the mid-nineteenth century, most physicians believed that disease spread through
miasmas
, poisonous vapors rising from filth and decay. Contemporaries were obsessed with air: moving to the countryside for the air, taking the air at the seaside. Bad air was blamed for sickness. Herbs were burned to purify the air to fight the plague. But because they didn’t understand what made the air dirty, they were not very good at cleaning it. This began to change only when Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch provided the first definitive proof that microscopic organisms were responsible for infectious disease.
Cleaning air relies on the same fundamental techniques as cleaning water: replacement, filtration, and disinfection. Pathogens replicate inside people, who then expel them into the air by breathing, talking, or coughing, where they can remain suspended and infect new individuals. The relative contributions of aerosol transmission, droplet transmission, and fomite (surface) transmission vary between diseases. Certain diseases, such as Covid-19, are driven by a small number of highly infectious individuals (‘superspreaders’) that account for a disproportionate number of cases.
In 1877
, British researchers Arthur Downes and Thomas Blunt stumbled upon a discovery that would lay the groundwork for modern disinfection. In
a paper
submitted to the Royal Society of London, they described how over the course of six months they had used sunlight to prevent bacteria from growing in a tube.
Follow-up research by Robert Koch demonstrated that sunlight could kill
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
, but the early experiments lacked precision. Scientists knew light worked, but not which parts of the spectrum were responsible. The turning point came in 1930, when Frederick L Gates
published
the first quantitative analysis of how ultraviolet light affected bacteria, pinpointing peak germicidal effectiveness at 265 nanometers, the same point that nucleic acids – DNA and RNA – absorb light.
Understanding the spectrum wasn’t necessary for harnessing it. In 1901, American electrical engineer Peter Cooper Hewitt
patented
the first mercury-vapor lamp to achieve widespread commercial success. Hewitt created a voltage difference across electrodes in a glass tube, with mercury vapor causing electrons to separate from mercury atoms and collide with other atoms, exciting them to higher energy states. When these excited atoms return to their ground state, they release energy as photons, primarily at a wavelength of 254 nanometers.
A Cooper Hewitt Mercury Lamp, 1903.
Image
Wikimedia Commons
.
Nucleic acids absorb this 254-nanometer light and produce new bonds between bases, preventing DNA/RNA replication. F
